Telegram — messages and buttons: Receives authenticated Telegram messages and callback_query updates. Native chat/user restrictions limit this private prototype to its owner.
Telegram identity: Maps sender ID, private chat ID, command, callback ID and Telegram update ID. Identity never comes from user message text.
Private test settings: Defines the owner allowlist, delivery switch, server timestamp and offer lifetime. One-minute TTL is used only for explicitly approved accelerated QA; the normal setting is ten minutes.
Private tester only: Rejects non-owner or non-private requests before reading or changing appointment state. Trusted manual storage tests use a separate synthetic branch.
Read appointment state: Reads exactly one scoped prototype row from the native n8n Data table. Missing or duplicate state rows fail closed.
Availability + booking rules: Pure deterministic service/bay capacity checks, appointment ownership, explicit waitlist consent, FIFO-compatible matching, holds, expiry, deduplication and paginated Telegram menus. No LLM and no network calls.
Commit only if revision unchanged: Writes the next state only when both row ID and expected revision still match. This is a conditional state update, not an unconditional overwrite.
Our commit succeeded: Verifies the returned revision and execution-specific commit token before any success message can be sent. Production concurrency stress testing remains a separate gate.
Verified delivery context: Restores the prepared messages and trusted routing context only after the state commit was verified.
Messages to send: Routes nonempty message batches to delivery. Silent expiry or synthetic storage checks finish without Telegram calls.
One recipient per message: Splits prepared replies and targeted offers into individual recipient items. This is not a subscriber broadcast.
Live delivery and tester allowlist: A second delivery gate checks the live switch, recipient allowlist and non-synthetic source before Telegram sendMessage.
Telegram — reply with inline buttons: Uses the native Telegram credential to send a message with four native inline buttons. Each label and callback has its own expression; variable menus use short pages.
Preview only — nothing sent: Produces a readable preview when live delivery is disabled or the recipient is not allowlisted. Does not send messages.
Storage smoke test PASSED: Reports a verified state roundtrip and zero messages sent for the manual synthetic storage branch.
No confirmation after storage conflict: Stops on a failed/ambiguous conditional commit. No false booking confirmation is emitted; reloading and a controlled retry are required.
Button needs acknowledgement: Detects real inline callbacks requiring an answerQuery acknowledgement. Ordinary text and synthetic events skip it.
Telegram — acknowledge button: Answers the inline callback to dismiss Telegram loading feedback. An acknowledgement failure is not a booking decision.
Ignore non-test users: Ends non-authorized/private-chat requests without a reply or state change.
Manual — storage smoke test: Starts a synthetic persistence-only check. It is not a replacement for a real Telegram end-to-end test.
Synthetic event — NO messages: Builds a synthetic sender and unique probe event. This branch is restored to storage-only mode after transport QA.
Every minute — expire offers: Scheduled sweep for due holds and newly eligible cancelled windows. Temporarily enabled only for approved private expiry QA; otherwise disabled in this handoff.
Trusted expiry event: Builds a server-owned timer event. End users cannot grant themselves the internal scheduler role through Telegram text.
